paragraphs.text: Whose office it is to take vengeance on the wicked.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: Show by effect that you are judge of the world to punish the wicked.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: That is, brag of their cruelty and oppression, or esteem themselves above all others.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: Seeing the Church was then so sore oppressed, it ought not to seem strange to us, if we see it so now, and therefore we must call to God, to take our cause in hand.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: He shows that they are desperate in malice, as they did not fear God, but gave themselves wholly to do wickedly.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: He shows that it is impossible, but God should hear, see, and understand their wickedness.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: If God punishes whole nations for their sins, it is mere folly for any one man or else a few to think that God will spare them.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: God has care over his, and chastised them for their own good, that they should not perish for ever with the wicked.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: God will restore the state and government of things to their right use, and then the godly will follow him cheerfully.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: He complains of them who would not help him to resist the enemies, yet was assured that God's help would not fail.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: When I thought there was no way but death.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: In my trouble and distress I always found your present help.
paragraphs.label: m
paragraphs.anchor: thoughts within me thy comforts delight

paragraphs.text: Though the wicked judges pretend justice in oppressing the Church, yet they do not have the authority of God.
paragraphs.label: n

paragraphs.text: It is a great token of God's judgment when the purpose of the wicked is broken, but most, when they are destroyed in their own malice.
